sponsor_or_proposer: Dangote Industries Limited (VP Devakumar Edwin quoted; Aliko Dangote)
current_state: Announced July 2025: Dangote submitted paperwork (late June 2025) for Nigeria's largest deep-sea seaport at Olokola, Ogun State, explicitly to anchor LNG exports, and stated intent to 'bring more gas than what NLNG is doing today' via new pipelines from the Niger Delta. Enabling infrastructure is advancing: the East-West Offshore Gas Gathering System (EWOGGS, twin 38-inch ~550 km offshore lines, Bonny to Lekki) has pipe orders placed with shipments arriving, and Olokola FTZ site mobilization was reported May 2026 with construction from Q4 2026 (refinery/fertilizer components). No FEED, permit, or capacity figure exists yet for the LNG liquefaction plant itself.
missing_threshold_elements: Location ambiguous for the LNG plant itself (reports split between Olokola port and the Lekki, Lagos industrial complex where EWOGGS terminates — fails the single-leading-site test); no concrete step specific to the liquefaction terminal (steps taken are for the port, FTZ, and pipeline); no stated LNG capacity. Sponsor is firmly identified.
watch_for: Confirmation of the liquefaction plant site (Olokola vs Lekki); an announced mtpa capacity; LNG-plant FEED award, NMDPRA licence-to-establish, or EIA; FID. If it firms up at Olokola, stage as a NEW terminal with AssociatedTerminals -> Olokola LNG Terminal (T100000130262) — different sponsor (Dangote vs NNPC) at/near the dead OK LNG site, per the dead-and-revived rule.
